newsitem.title: USA: Dlr near highs late in US, eyeing upside anew.
newsitem.headline: Dlr near highs late in US, eyeing upside anew.

text.p: The dollar ended higher on Tuesday, climbing to a 2-1/2-month high against the yen and recouping most of its brief losses against the mark.
Dollar/yen climbed to 118.45 -- its highest level since 119.15 on May 14 -- largely on momentum after the pair took out a key technical retracement level at 117.00.
Traders said dollar/yen now was within reach of the next main resistance at 119.00, the 50-percent retracement of the 1997 high/low move between 126.47 and 110.62.
In late trade, dollar/yen was quoted at 118.35/45, up from 117.60/65 at the open.
Meanwhile, dollar/mark that had surged on Monday to 1.8490, its highest since November 1989, fell to a session low of 1.8265, essentially due to profit-taking.
However, dollar/mark rebounded quickly as frustrated bears were met with solid interest to buy in the dip. Dealers said this signaled fresh gains ahead for that pair.
Late Tuesday, the dollar traded at 1.8375/85 marks versus 1.8315/25 at the open.
"Heavy selling out of Europe today failed to break the dollar's back," said Stephen Flanagan, senior dealer at Credit Agricole Indosuez.
Concern that Germany may tighten credit this summer prompted the dollar/mark selling in Europe, traders said.
That concern was tied to the Bundesbank's decision on July 24, at its last meeting before its four-week summer recession, to fix Germany's 3.0-percent repo rate for two weeks only.
Traders said this could be read as meaning German repo rates could become variable in mid-August and drift higher.

Some confusion among players also resulted from comments by Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick who said the German central bank must be very careful when assessing the weak mark versus the weak German economy.
Some market players interpreted Koebnick's comments a hint of higher German interest rates ahead.

However, the U.S. unit's ability to hold firmly above support at 1.8250 -- the 38-percent retracement of the rally from 1.7860 on July 21 to the high of 1.8490 on Monday -- convinced the bulls to resume long dollar/mark positions.

Dealers said the main news of the day had little impact on trading. First, the second-quarter U.S. Employment Cost Index came in as expected at up 0.8 percent, confirming the absence of wage-driven inflation and the market's view that the Federal Reserve will keep policy steady in the near term.
The dollar was not moved either by news of a deal reached by the Clinton administration and Republican leaders in Congress to balance the U.S. federal budget by 2002.
Market players agreed the dollar still has enough stamina to push higher against both the mark and the yen this summer.
However, some cautioned the dollar upside may be limited at the key psychological level of 120 yen where they expected verbal intervention to stem the yen slide.
As for dollar/mark, some dealers wondered how far Germany was prepared to let the mark depreciate versus the dollar before intervening in the market or raising interest rates.
"Koebnick said if dollar/mark gets a lot higher, they would start to become more forceful with (rates,)" said Mark Gargano, chief dealer at First Union National Bank.

Dollar/Swiss retreated briefly but held above support at 1.5030 Swiss francs -- the 38-percent retracement of the July 18-28 rally from 1.4690 to Monday's four-year high of 1.5250. Dollar/Swiss closed at 1.5178/88 vs. 1.5155/60 at the open.
The dollar also ended at Canadian $1.3848/53 vs. C$1.3844/49. Cable closed at $1.6282/92 vs. $1.6313/23 and the Australian dollar at $0.7447/52 vs. $0.7408/18.
(( -- Al Yoon, N.A. Forex Unit, 212-859-1672 ))
